style_when: the story turns on one physical thing — a part, a material, a component, a document — and what that thing costs, contains or crosses a border is the news
prompt: Extreme asymmetric macro photograph on a weathered asphalt shingle roof plane: a 15-year-old charcoal-grey shingle with a lifted, curling tab edge sits low on the left third, loose ceramic granules drifted in the course seam. Low late-afternoon sun rakes hard from the left, pulling long shadow lines off every lifted edge and exposing worn bald patches and rust-coloured lichen. Receding shingle courses fall away into soft blur toward bone-white sky in the upper right, generous editorial negative space. 100mm macro lens, razor-thin focal plane locked on the curling tab, visible granule texture and dust, fine film grain. Charcoal, rust and bone-white palette. No people, no text, no logos.
rationale: The story literally turns on one physical material — the aging asphalt shingle — and what that material's age now costs, which is the exact brief for a macro. A 100mm plane at inspection distance makes every lifted tab and lost granule read as the contested evidence in the ARMA–IBHS fight. Architectural night would bury the roof's age in silhouette and studio object would read as a product catalog for a policy story.
subject: a weathered asphalt shingle roof surface with lifted, curling tab edges and drifted loose granules
core_thesis: From January 1, 2027, an asphalt roof past 15 years loses the FORTIFIED designation behind insurance discounts, and the shingle industry is publicly calling the science behind that age ceiling flawed.
core_conflict: Shingle makers' claim of long service life versus insurers converting roof age into eligibility cutoffs and drop letters — the certificate expires while the roof may still hold years of usable life.
composition: extreme asymmetric close-up — the curling shingle tab anchors the lower-left third while receding courses fall away into soft blur toward bone-white sky in the upper right
